intended_object: A plain type equivalence between the one-field wrapper structure `v.Completion` and its underlying type `v.1.Completion` (the completion of K at the absolute value of v). The docstring describes it as packaging the constructor and projection as an equivalence.
explanation: `v.Completion` is a one-field structure wrapping `v.1.Completion`. It exists only to keep the instances separate. `equivCompletion` is the bare `Equiv` given by the projection `toCompletion` and the constructor `ofCompletion`, and both inverse laws hold by `rfl`. The library uses it only to move structure across the wrapper; for example, the next line defines the `NormedField` instance with `(equivCompletion v).normedField`. Mathematically the two types are the same object, so this equivalence is an implementation detail with no counterpart in the literature. It is correct for what it is meant to do.
